chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sayf al-Tammarr, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'We used to perform Hajj on foot, but something from you reached us, so what is your view?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The people perform Hajj on foot and they ride.' I said, 'I am not asking you about that.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Then about what did you ask?' I said, 'Which of the two is more beloved to you that we should do?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Riding is more beloved to me, for that is stronger for you in supplication and worship.'
ai.seo_question: Is it better to perform Hajj on foot or by riding according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while walking is valid, riding is preferred because it preserves the pilgrim's physical strength, thereby enhancing their capacity for *dua* and *ibadah*. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *islah al-jasad* (well-being of the body) as a means to facilitate greater spiritual devotion, rather than viewing ascetic hardship as an end in itself. The preference underscores the practical wisdom of maintaining energy levels to maximize the quality of worship during the Hajj rituals.
